status_summary: On the ESA side, FWS and NMFS jointly proposed rescinding the regulatory definition of harm on 2025-04-17 and published the final rescission on 2026-07-14, removing the definition from 50 CFR parts 17 and 222, the latter covering NMFS marine species; the rule took effect on 2026-09-14 and is in force. On 2025-11-21 the two agencies also proposed revising the listing and critical habitat rules (50 CFR part 424) and the interagency consultation rules (part 402) by restoring 2019 text; neither is final. On the MMPA side, NOAA Fisheries published an advance notice on 2026-07-29 seeking comment on revising its fish and fish product import regulations; no change to MMPA take, deterrence or subsistence rules was found. In responses to comments the final harm rule addresses Tribal subsistence and treaty fishing by stating that ESA requirements are separate from treaty rights, and it makes no subsistence-specific change.

title: Modify MMPA and ESA regulations said to burden fisheries and Native subsistence
uncertainties: The final harm rule was read in full in two parts; its fisheries discussion is general (incidental catch examples and comments on commercial and sport fishing), and it does not mention the MMPA. The April 2025 harm proposal and the November 2025 proposals were identified from Federal Register listings and not reread here. Lawsuits against the harm rescission filed in 2026 are tracked in c16-05 and were not reviewed. A Federal Register query of proposed rules mentioning MMPA import provisions since 2025-01-20 showed species-specific incidental take rules but no general change to take, deterrence or subsistence rules; the query was not exhaustive. Whether the import provisions are among the regulations the text says burden U.S. fisheries is a judgment. Overlap: the harm rescission and the part 424 proposal are also counted in c16-05 (Interior chapter); this record covers the Commerce side and the MMPA. In this pass the Federal Register API metadata confirmed 90 FR 16102 (proposed harm rescission, comments to 2025-05-19), 91 FR 43300 (final, effective 2026-09-14, 50 CFR parts 17 and 222), 90 FR 52607 (part 424 proposal, comments to 2025-12-22), 90 FR 52600 (part 402 proposal) and 91 FR 47798 (MMPA import advance notice, comments to 2026-09-28, 50 CFR part 216); the full text of the final rule was read in a later review.
